message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 130, "amount_cents": 8178}, {"order_id": 133, "amount_cents": 10961}, {"order_id": 134, "amount_cents": 8998}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work. I'll start by listing the refunds in the shared ledger and comparing them against the handoff.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff exactly (orders 130, 133, 134 with the same amounts). Next I'll list the orders to identify the customers before checking net balances.
The ledger's refunds match Alpha's handoff, and each refund is smaller than its order amount, so nothing looks wrong. Next I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme.

Acme's net balance of 24701 matches my own check: orders 17595 + 26245 = 43840, minus refunds 8178 + 10961 = 19139, gives 24701. The refund ledger matches Alpha's handoff, so I'll record Acme's payout.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch is next, so I'll get its net balance from the ledger rather than computing it myself.
Birch's net balance of 61735 matches my check: orders 37666 + 33067 = 70733, minus refund 8998 on order 134 = 61735. The refunds are verified, so I'll record Birch's payout.
Acme and Birch are paid. Cobalt is the last customer, with orders 132 and 135 and no refunds in the ledger. I'll get its net balance from the ledger.
Cobalt has orders 132 (10547) and 135 (6294) and no refunds in the ledger, so the expected net is 16841. That matches the ledger's net_balance, so I'll record Cobalt's payout.
All three customers have been paid. I verified Alpha's refunds against the ledger and checked each net balance against my own arithmetic before recording the payouts.
